From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GPU runway: weekly sync — pipeline-driven sizing ask

Team —

Linking sales, finance and infra for our weekly fleet planning touchpoint. I pulled last week's pipeline snapshots and sketched two quick sizing scenarios for ACME (attached): a conservative ramp and an aggressive ramp that assumes pilot -> paid in 8 weeks. Please review the attachment (fleet_weekly_packet_v2.xlsx) before EOD Monday.

Ask:
- Marissa: can you confirm which opportunities in the HubSpot deal (ACME-2027-0567) are expected to close inside the 8-week aggressive window? A short prioritized list with expected start dates will do.
- Ben: any infra constraints we should assume (GPU families, preemption tolerance) if we need to push burst capacity?
- Laura: finance — does the aggressive scenario line up with the expected commit / billing cadence this quarter? If there are any revenue recognition flags, flag them here.

I've pasted the executive summary below. Full workbook attached.

--- Executive summary ---
Conservative: reserve 12 A100-equivalent slots across two pools, start in 6 weeks, burst up to +25% for 3 weeks.
Aggressive: reserve 36 A100-equivalent slots, start in 2–3 weeks; requires prioritized burst credits and potential pre-provisioning in us-west.

Attachments: fleet_weekly_packet_v2.xlsx (sizing worksheets), acme_pipeline_snapshot.csv (export from HubSpot)

Thanks,
Hiro
Hiro Tanaka
Head of Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference

Thanks Hiro — quick responses inline and a short attach (acme_pipeline_snapshot.csv) updated with likely start dates.

- ACME OPPS that matter for the 8-week aggressive window:
  * ACME-CorePilot (50% prob) — internal pilot kickoff targeted 2027-06-10; expected 6-week pilot then convert to paid.
  * ACME-SearchEmbed (30% prob) — proof-of-concept, 2027-06-20 start, likely limited capacity needs (20% of pilot).
  * ACME-Platform (20% prob) — larger, but unlikely before Q3.

I've shaded the workbook rows where we should prioritize sloting. If we take the aggressive sizing we should hold a small burst pool (8–10 slots) reserved for the CorePilot week-1.

Other notes:
- Nora from ACME confirmed procurement is ready to move once we get final SOW and committed start date. She pinged procurement@acme.ai today.
- HubSpot link: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/ACME-2027-0567 — I updated close date to 2027-06-15 for planning; please treat as optimistic.

Marissa
Marissa Cole

+1 on the aggressive plan if sales can firm the CorePilot date. A couple of infra notes:
- Preferred families: we can support either A100 or H100 quantized flow; A100 is slightly cheaper for embed-heavy workloads.
- Preemption tolerance: ACME said the pilot can tolerate spot/preemptible instances for non-latency critical work, but they want reserved for inference queries (p99 target).
- Burst path: we have ~18 burstable slots available in us-west that can be reallocated if finance signs off.

I'll flag the 18 slots as potential burst but require a written commit window from finance (Laura).

Ben
